meta.triageRationale: One optional input on one existing tool plus one optional parameter on its read helper; one obvious approach.

summary.prose: git_ls_files gets one optional integer input, maxBytes (1 to 52428800), that sets how much output the listing may hold. Without it nothing changes: the 10 MiB default of the shell helper still applies. A listing over the budget stays a rejected failure and is never returned cut. readGit gains the matching optional parameter, and git_rev_parse and git_hash_object now fail on a cut capture instead of reading a cut line (added to this Story on 2026-10-27); no other git tool or caller changes. The consumer is Story s9's ignore filter, which needs 50 MiB.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Add an optional output budget to git_ls_files

parameters.name: maxBytes
parameters.purpose: The most stdout the listing may produce; the default is runShell's 10 MiB.

dataModelChanges.details: One optional field maxBytes (integer, minimum 1, maximum 52428800). The schema stays additionalProperties false, so a caller that does not know the field is unaffected and a caller that sends it on an older daemon is refused by that daemon's schema.

errorCases.scenario: The listing is longer than the budget
errorCases.detection: runShell sets stdoutTruncated when stdoutBytes passes maxBytes (src/daemon/tools/shell-helper.ts:207) and parseOutput returns the rejected failure 'git output was cut at the byte limit' (src/daemon/tools/builtins/git/parsers.ts:24)
errorCases.response: The failure is returned; no files are returned and the cut text rides only on failure.original.
errorCases.userImpact: The ignore filter degrades to permissive with its warning, as it does today past 50 MiB.

errorCases.scenario: maxBytes is zero, negative, not an integer or above 52428800
errorCases.detection: The input is checked against the tool's input schema (Type.Integer with minimum 1 and maximum 52428800) before execute runs
errorCases.response: The call is refused as an invalid input and no command runs.
errorCases.userImpact: The caller sees the schema's message.

errorCases.scenario: git ls-files fails or is not installed
errorCases.detection: readGit returns a failure for a spawn error or a non-zero exit (helpers.ts:107-108)

errorCases.scenario: git_rev_parse or git_hash_object prints more than the capture holds
errorCases.detection: runShell sets stdoutTruncated (src/daemon/tools/shell-helper.ts:207); the tool passes its read through parseOutput (src/daemon/tools/builtins/git/parsers.ts:19), which fails a cut capture
errorCases.response: A rejected failure 'git output was cut at the byte limit' and no data. Before this change neither tool checked for a cut capture: git_rev_parse split the cut text into values and returned success, and git_hash_object checked only that the retained text is an object name, so it failed when the retained text was something else and succeeded when the retained text was a valid object name followed by dropped output (runShell keeps whole chunks and drops the rest).
errorCases.userImpact: A caller never receives cut values as if they were whole; outputs of one line or a few lines never reach the limit, so no existing use changes.

edgeCases.expected: The call is exactly the call made today, under runShell's 10 MiB.

edgeCases.input: A listing of exactly maxBytes bytes
edgeCases.expected: Accepted: runShell appends while stdoutBytes is at most maxBytes.

edgeCases.input: A listing one byte over maxBytes

edgeCases.expected: The same files as without it.

edgeCases.input: A unicode file name that counts more bytes than characters
edgeCases.expected: The budget counts bytes, as runShell does.

invariantsToPreserve.text: A listing that does not fit is a failure and is never returned cut.
The six readGit callers other than git_ls_files (git_ls_tree, git_rev_parse, git_for_each_ref, git_path_history, git_rev_list and git_hash_object) pass no maxBytes and keep runShell's 10 MiB default.
git_ls_files keeps its tool id, its other inputs, its arguments (--literal-pathspecs, -z, --exclude-standard with others or ignored) and the NUL check on paths.

git_rev_parse and git_hash_object keep their inputs, argv, timeouts and results for output that fits the capture; only a cut capture changes, from a cut success (rev-parse), or a success or an object-name failure depending on the retained text (hash-object), to the one cut-capture failure.

migration.stateBefore: git_ls_files has inputs cwd, paths, cached, others and ignored and reads under runShell's 10 MiB default; readGit takes no byte budget (s1 bundle 1). A listing over the budget is a rejected failure (s1 bundle 2). The consumer, createRepoIgnoreFilter, allows 50 MiB (s1 bundle 3).
migration.stateAfter: git_ls_files also accepts an optional maxBytes (1 to 52428800) that readGit hands to runShell. Without it every call is as before. A listing over the budget is still a rejected failure. git_rev_parse and git_hash_object also fail on a cut capture; no other tool or readGit caller changes. git_rev_parse and git_hash_object fail on a cut capture.

migrationSteps.action: Add the optional maxBytes parameter to readGit and pass it into the runShell options.
Add the optional maxBytes input to git_ls_files and pass it to readGit.
Make git_rev_parse and git_hash_object read their output through parseOutput, so a cut capture is the one failure; keep their other behaviour.
Add the new test file, extend the coverage test, and run the git suites and the typecheck.

migration.backwardCompat: Additive: a new optional input on git_ls_files and a new optional last parameter on readGit. Existing calls, the tool id, the other inputs and the six other readGit callers are unchanged, and the default budget is unchanged. A caller that sends maxBytes to a daemon built before this change is refused by that daemon's schema (additionalProperties false). One behaviour change, for output over the 10 MiB capture only: git_rev_parse returned the cut text split into values as a success, and git_hash_object succeeded or failed with a different message depending on the retained text; both now fail with the cut-capture message. One-line and few-line outputs never reach that size.

alternativesConsidered.name: Optional maxBytes input on git_ls_files, passed through readGit
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: git_ls_files takes an optional integer maxBytes (1 to 52428800); readGit takes an optional maxBytes and hands it to runShell.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add `maxBytes: Type.Optional(Type.Integer({ minimum: 1, maximum: 52428800 }))` to the input schema of src/daemon/tools/builtins/git/ls-files.ts. execute reads it and passes it to readGit, whose new optional last parameter (after signal) goes into the runShell options. When it is absent nothing changes (runShell's 10 MiB default). A listing over the budget is already a rejected failure through parseOutput ('git output was cut at the byte limit'), never a cut result. Separately, git_rev_parse and git_hash_object read through parseOutput so a cut capture is a failure; no other tool and no other readGit caller changes.
pros: Smallest change that meets the Story: one input, one optional parameter, behaviour unchanged by default.
Reuses runShell's maxBytes and parseOutput's failure on a cut; no new failure kind.
The consumer chooses its own budget (50 MiB) and every other caller keeps 10 MiB.
cons: A caller can ask for up to 50 MiB of memory for one read; the ceiling is fixed in the schema.
Another input on the tool that agents see.

alternativesConsidered.name: Raise git_ls_files' fixed budget to 50 MiB
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Give git_ls_files a fixed 50 MiB read budget with no new input.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Pass a constant 50 MiB maxBytes from ls-files.ts to readGit for every call; no input is added.
pros: No new input; the consumer needs nothing extra.
cons: Changes the behaviour of the tool for every existing caller and agent: a large listing that failed at 10 MiB now holds up to 50 MiB in memory.
Hides the budget from the caller, who cannot ask for less.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates the optional-input and unchanged-default requirements (req1, req2).

alternativesConsidered.name: A budget option on every readGit tool
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add the same optional maxBytes to the other readGit-based tools (rev-list, ls-tree, path-history and others).
alternativesConsidered.approach: Give every tool that calls readGit an optional maxBytes input and pass it through, so the family is uniform.
pros: One uniform option across the read tools.
Later consumers with large outputs need no further change.
cons: Seven tools change for one consumer's need, and each needs its own tests and schema entry.
Adds an option nobody has asked for on six tools.
Widens the Story past its stated scope ('no other git tool changes').
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates the stated scope (req4) and multiplies the test surface (req5).

The originating request is the Story's userValue text (the user's 2026-10-27 answer 'A' to add the budget option for Story s9 of the one-tool-registry epic).
Whether any test pins the input-schema field list of git tools was not read; the build should search for one (a table of inputs per tool) before adding the field.
Alternative scoring (alt2): there are no Story criteria, shared contracts or Epic constraints, so the alternatives were scored against five requirements read from the Story text (req1 to req5).

Review round 1 corrected the caller count: readGit( appears eight times including its definition, so seven tools call it and six besides git_ls_files (git_ls_tree, git_rev_parse, git_for_each_ref, git_path_history, git_rev_list and git_hash_object); the regression test names all six. The content was changed by hand through the lifecycle service, revision 2, and is not yet re-reviewed.

Scope extended on 2026-10-27 at the user's request (after the first build of this Story): git_rev_parse and git_hash_object now fail on a cut capture. Neither tool checked for a cut capture before: git_rev_parse returned cut text as a success, and git_hash_object succeeded when the retained text was a valid object name followed by dropped output and otherwise failed with an object-name message (review round 3 corrected an earlier claim that it always failed). The ac6 above covers it. The content was changed by hand through the lifecycle service (revision 3) and is not yet re-reviewed; the BUILD already made for revisions 1 and 2 needs the extra change, a new gate run and a new code review.
